title: hardware-comparison-benchmarks-a100-h100-l40s-cloud-skus-cuda-drivers-brief
body:
Summary:

This doc records the hardware comparison runs we executed in Feb 2026 to investigate serving-runtime performance differences across NVIDIA A100, H100, and L40S across cloud SKUs and CUDA/driver versions. Goal: characterize throughput, p99 latency, and memory/KV-cache behavior for representative 7B and 70B transformer models and produce actionable recommendations for default platform configs and image/container driver compatibility.

High-level outcome (short):
- H100 (p5-class) shows best single-request p99 latency for long-context 70B workloads and highest tokens/sec for fp16/amp runs, but requires CUDA 12.x and a recent driver to unlock TensorFloat-32/Triton kernels - we observed 10-25% better throughput vs A100 on the 70B tests when using optimized kernels.
- A100 (p4d/a2) remains cost-effective for 7B and many 13B workloads; performance is stable across CUDA 11.8+ driver combos.
- L40S (newer L-class) provides good density and lower power but showed regression in our large-batch KV cache memory behavior on some cloud SKUs (likely driver/kernel mismatch); needs careful CUDA 12.1+ validation.

Test matrix (runs included):
- Models: 7B decoder-only (redwood-7b-rlhf), 70B decoder-only (redwood-70b-v1).
- Batch sizes: 1 (latency), 8, 32 (throughput).
- Sequence lengths: 64 (short), 512 (medium), 2048 (long).
- Precision/configs: fp16 (AMP), int8-quantized (where supported), bf16 on H100 where available.
- Cloud SKUs tested: AWS p4d.24xlarge (A100), AWS p5.48xlarge (H100), GCP a2-highgpu-8g (A100-like), Azure ND A100 v4 (A100), GCP a3p-16g L40S (L40S preview), Azure L40S preview VM (L40S).
- Driver/CUDA combos: NVIDIA driver 525 + CUDA 11.8, driver 535 + CUDA 12.1, driver 545 + CUDA 12.2 (where available). cuDNN/cuBLAS versions noted per run.

Methodology / harness notes:
- All runs executed using the same docker image baseline: redwood/serving-runtime:perf-2026-02 with pinned python, torch-nightly (custom build), and the runtime compiled against the target CUDA for that node (we build images per CUDA version).
- Microbenchmarks: token-generation steady-state measured across 10-minute steady windows after a 2-minute warmup. We record tokens/sec, mean latency, p95, p99, GPU memory alloc high-water mark, GPU utilization, and power draw when available.
- Profiling: nvprof/nvtx traces for representative runs; Nsight Systems for full end-to-end tracing on selected combinations. Kernel-level timings were extracted and aggregated.
- KV-cache stress: long-context streaming (2048) with repeated prefixes to exercise KV cache eviction/lookup.
- All runs seeded and repeated 3x; reported numbers are median of successful runs. Logs and raw traces uploaded to S3 (linked above).

Representative results (median across 3 runs) - short summary table (numbers approximate):

7B model, seq=512, batch=8, fp16:
- AWS p4d (A100) CUDA 11.8: 18.5k tokens/sec, p99=28ms, GPU mem used 23GB
- GCP a2 (A100) CUDA 11.8: 17.9k tokens/sec, p99=30ms, GPU mem used 24GB
- AWS p5 (H100) CUDA 12.1: 21.3k tokens/sec, p99=24ms, GPU mem used 22GB
- GCP L40S (a3p) CUDA 12.1: 19.6k tokens/sec, p99=27ms, GPU mem used 21GB (note: occasional KV cache thrash)

70B model, seq=2048, batch=1, fp16 (long-context, latency-sensitive):
- AWS p4d (A100) CUDA 11.8: tokens/sec ~320, p99=680ms, GPU mem used 38GB
- AWS p5 (H100) CUDA 12.1: tokens/sec ~410, p99=540ms, GPU mem used 36GB (optimized kernels enabled)
- Azure ND A100 v4 CUDA 11.8: tokens/sec ~300, p99=720ms
- L40S (GCP preview) CUDA 12.1: tokens/sec ~360, p99=600ms but observed 1/6 runs with 10-20% slowdown due to a kernel fallback path

Notes on driver/CUDA effects:
- H100 requires CUDA 12.x to utilize certain TF32/RGEMM optimizations in our custom kernels. On CUDA 11.x builds, we observed kernel fallbacks that reduced throughput by ~15-25% for 70B runs.
- A100 shows robust perf on CUDA 11.8; moving to CUDA 12.1/12.2 did not significantly change throughput for fp16 on our baseline kernels, but some vendor libs improved small-batch latency slightly.
- L40S seems to be sensitive to a driver mismatch: older drivers triggered a fallback path in cuBLAS for int8/bf16 kernels. Ensure distro drivers >= 535 and CUDA >= 12.1 when targeting L40S.

Profiling observations (interesting hotspots):
- KV-cache copy/concat overhead dominates CPU-side time when batch > 8 for long-context sequences; we need to revisit the memcpy/packing code path and consider pinned-memory async staging.
- For H100 runs, kernel launches for attention had higher occupancy but better arithmetic throughput; however there were some synchronization stalls (~3-5% time) in cross-device NCCL collectives on p5 multi-GPU nodes when we enabled tensor-slicing parallelism.
- A100 shows higher consistent SM utilization; H100 peaks higher but more bursty.

Stability/regressions observed:
- L40S preview VMs on GCP had an intermittent driver bug where per-process GPU memory accounting was slightly underreported; this led to OOM-like behavior in one 70B run. Repro steps and logs are uploaded.
- H100 on older CUDA 11.x images led to kernel fallbacks and reproducible throughput regressions; we recommend gating H100 images on CUDA 12.1+ images.

Recommendations (operational):
1) Default runtime images: ship two images for customers/auto-detect:
   - cuda-11.8 runtime (stable, default) for A100/backcompat workloads
   - cuda-12.1 runtime (optimized) for H100/L40S workloads where customers request the new SKU or the runtime detects H100/L40S at startup
2) Image selection logic: on node boot, query GPU model via nvidia-smi and select runtime variant; fail to start with clear error if driver < required.
3) KV-cache optimizations: implement async pinned-memory staging for KV packing and overlap with GPU compute; this should reduce CPU-side tail latency for batch >= 8.
4) Driver validation tests: add quick smoke tests in init-phase that check cuBLAS kernel variants for int8/bf16 to detect driver fallbacks on L40S.
5) Release note: document that H100 requires CUDA 12.1+ to reach advertised perf for large models.

Next steps / open questions:
- Follow-up runs with int8-quantized 70B on H100 (using our new quant toolchain) to measure cost-per-token improvements and stability.
- Re-run L40S matrix after driver 545+ is available on GCP preview to confirm kernel fallback fixes.
- Investigate NCCL cross-GPU stalls on p5 when enabling tensor-slicing; open a ticket with vendor if we can reproduce with a minimal repro.

Notes to reviewers:
- Logs and raw traces are in S3 (linked). The harness and exact command lines are in PR #482.
- Many of the runs were done on ephemeral preview machines (GCP L40S) - treat those numbers as preliminary until we re-run on GA SKUs.
- If we adopt dual-image strategy, ops will need an image promotion checklist and a migration plan for existing Dedicated clusters.

Appendix (quick checklist for reproducing one run):
1) Checkout PR: git checkout pr/482
2) Build image: ./build-image.sh --cuda 12.1 --tag perf-2026-02
3) Launch node (example AWS): aws ec2 run-instances --instance-type p5.48xlarge --image-id ami-...
4) Start harness: ./run-benchmark.sh --model redwood-70b-v1 --seq 2048 --batch 1 --precision fp16 --duration 600

-- Ava
